la:verb:suesco.gloss: to become used or accustomed to
senses: to become used or accustomed to
la:verb:suesco.html:
sŭesco, sŭēvi, sŭētum (dissyl. suēvi, suētum; sync. forms, suesti, suerunt, suesse, etc.;
v.in the foll., and cf. also the preced. art.), 3, v. inch. n. and a. [Sanscr. svadhā, will, might, custom; Gr. ἔθος, ἦθος].
Neutr., to become used or accustomed; in the tempp. perff., to have accustomed one's self; hence, to be wont, used, or accustomed (rare).
Tempp. press.: Drusus in Illyricum missus est, ut suesceret militiae,; ; .—
Tempp. perff.: has Graeci stellas Hyadas vocitare suërunt, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 43, 111: a te id, quod suesti, peto, etc.,: mittere suevit,: de divis dare dicta suërit,: gemmis florere arbusta suësse,: vincere suevit,sueverat claustra remoliri,.—
Act., to accustom, habituate, train (very rare in finite verb): ut lectos viros ... disciplinae et imperiis suesceret,. —Esp., P. and P. a.: suētus, a, um.
Accustomed, wont, used, habituated; with inf.: ex aliis sentire sueti,: mala secundis rebus oriri sueta, ap. , 2, 18: suetus abstinere,: curru succedere sueti Quadrupedes,: vexare suëtae,: comitialem propter morbum despui suetum,.—With dat.: his (armis) ego suetus,: neque conjugiis suscipiendis neque alendis liberis sueti,: suetae aquis volucres,: sueti latrociniis,: suetus civilibus armis,. —
Transf., of things, customary, usual (mostly post-class.): contra Cheruscis sueta aput paludes proelia,: sueto militum contubernio gaudere,; vestigium,: cibaria,, p. 232, 13.—Hence, subst.: suē-tum, i, n., a custom, usage: se ad sectae sueta conferunt,.
